message.content:
Lions (family Felidae) and zebras (family Equidae) are both members of the super‑order **Laurasiatheria**.  
Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of the Laurasiatheria clade – a small, insectivorous mammal that lived roughly 70 million years ago, long after the split of the placental mammals but before the divergence of the carnivore and horse lineages.
